subject: Oceanography
title: Coral Bleaching
description: A micro-lesson that makes Coral Bleaching usable.

hook.text: Corals turn white when stressed by heat—expelling the algae that give them color and 90% of their food.

buildup.text: Just 1–2°C above normal summer maximums triggers bleaching—and sustained heat kills the coral entirely.

discovery.text: Mass bleaching events were unknown before 1983—now they hit every few years, driven by warming seas.

twist.text: The 2024 global bleaching event was the most widespread ever recorded—affecting reefs in every ocean basin.

climax.text: If warming reaches 2°C, models predict 99% of coral reefs will experience annual bleaching—most won't survive.

punchline.text: Corals are the canary in the coal mine—and they're turning white.

quiz.question: What causes coral bleaching?
options: Heat stress makes corals expel their symbiotic algae
